summary: The per-process-salted Python hash() that maps each candidate spec's target_achievements to Achievement enums (stored as BaseTask.relevant_achievements) defines the task REWARD mask, early TERMINATION (task_solved), and SUCCESS criterion used during PPO training. It therefore enters reward, termination, success, and the PPO loss -- it is NOT a report-only label. Observation conditioning in this launcher uses a task-index one-hot (jnp.eye), so the salted achievements do not directly enter the policy embedding, but the task-index routes to tasks whose reward/termination are salted.

salt_site.code: ta = [_all_a[hash(f"{cid}_{a}") % len(_all_a)] for a in ta_names]
salt_site.note: Python str hash() is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED); mapping is unrecoverable and differs across runs.

call_chain_to_training: launch_d052_pure_dynamic_enhanced.py:1169 task_embeddings = jnp.eye(len(task_classes))  [task-INDEX one-hot, not salted achievements]
minicraftax/envs/multitask.py:324 self.reward_fns = tuple(t.get_reward for t in self.tasks)
minicraftax/envs/multitask.py:325 self.terminal_fns = tuple(t.is_terminal for t in self.tasks)

observation_conditioning.detail: launcher passes task_embeddings=jnp.eye(n) (task-index one-hot); ppo_tr.py:68 uses the passed embeddings. The salted relevant_achievements multi-hot path (_generate_embeddings_for_session one-hot branch, training/__init__.py:335-337) is NOT used by this launcher. NOTE: task-index still routes to a task whose reward/termination are salted.

eval_pilot.self_label: SUCCESS_MODE = "UNDEFINED"  # enhanced: relevant_ach via salted hash(), unrecoverable
eval_pilot.note: The per-episode eval itself flags success as UNDEFINED. Empirical per-achievement completion (used by the Modeler) is real/canonical and NOT salted.

consequence: Because hash() is per-process-salted, relevant_achievements (hence each task's reward function, termination, and success) is an effectively RANDOM achievement assignment, decoupled from the spec target_achievements labels the LLM judged. Curriculum selection (label-based) and training reward/termination/success (salt-based) are decoupled. Any training run (incl. a 4096 smoke) on these enhanced candidates trains on salted-random reward functions, making curriculum-quality conclusions uninterpretable until targets are made canonical.
base_paths_verified: src on sys.path = workers/gpu0_original/gpu0_training_mechanisms/src (launcher L99); base_task.py read from that tree.

reasons: PYTHONHASHSEED only makes hash() reproducible WITHIN a fixed process/seed; it does not make the target_achievements->Achievement mapping CORRECT. The mapping is still an arbitrary modulo projection of a string hash onto the achievement list, decoupled from the spec semantics the LLM judged.
A fixed seed freezes ONE random assignment; it does not recover the intended canonical targets, so reward/termination/success remain semantically wrong (just reproducibly wrong).
Cross-process/cross-machine reproducibility is fragile (interpreter/build dependent); relying on it for training semantics is unsafe.

Correct repair = an explicit, reversible, semantic mapping from each candidate's target_achievements to canonical Achievement enums (e.g. a curated name->enum table), validated so is_terminal/is_success/get_reward act on the REAL goals; then re-run eval so SUCCESS_MODE is computable (not UNDEFINED).
